name: clac
desc: Command-line, stack-based calculator with postfix notation
why: A stack-based postfix calculator is a small, old-school oddity that rewards a few minutes of play.

brief.what_it_is: clac is a command-line calculator that uses a stack and postfix (reverse Polish) notation. You type numbers and operators, and it pushes numbers onto a stack and pops arguments for each operation. Its interactive mode shows the full stack and updates it as you type each key. It can also run non-interactively: passing an expression as an argument prints the resulting stack, one value per line, top first. Operations include arithmetic, modulo, exponentiation, logs, trig, erf, factorial, rounding, bitwise and/or/xor, stack manipulation, and a stash. Users can define their own words in a config file.
brief.why_it_exists: The author likes Forth and other stack-based concatenative languages and has used the dc calculator a lot. He found other calculators less powerful than dc, and felt dc's UI was lacking, so he wanted to try an always-visible stack with realtime updates.
brief.how_it_works: Each number pushes onto the stack, and each operator pops its fixed number of arguments and pushes the result, so no parentheses or precedence rules are needed. In interactive mode the stack is redrawn on every keystroke. Operations that take a count, such as add and mul, pop a value a and then remove that many items from the stack. Words defined in the words file are aliases that expand to other operations and can be used like built-in commands.

brief.install_notes: Download the latest release from the GitHub releases page or check the distribution packages wiki page. You can also compile the source on the master branch. Build and install are done with make install, which puts clac in /usr/local/bin unless PREFIX is set. Beyond that, no runtime, accounts, or hardware are mentioned. Optional configuration: a words file at $CLAC_WORDS, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/clac/words, or $HOME/.config/clac/words. It is not created by default.
brief.standout: The always-visible stack that redraws on every keystroke makes the stack state the main interface, not just an answer. Words defined as simple aliases in a plain text file, plus a stash for temporarily moving stack items, give it a Forth-like flavor in a small CLI tool.
brief.status: unknown. The README has no release dates, version numbers, or notes about maintenance status, and I did not check the releases page or commit history. The README does link to a releases page and a packages wiki, and it accepts bug reports through issues.
brief.caveats: The README does not name a license, a supported platform list, or build requirements beyond make. Installing via make targets /usr/local/bin by default. Words are not created by default and must be set up by hand. Subtraction and division pop in an order that may be surprising (for example, - computes second-from-top minus top). The README says there are no inline comments in the words file. Arithmetic is not documented for overflow or precision beyond the example outputs.
quotes: A command line, stack-based calculator with postfix notation that displays the stack contents at all times.
I like Forth and other stack based, concatenative languages, and I've used the `dc` calculator a lot.
That's why I decided to try this idea of an always-visible stack with realtime updates.
